settings.label: Font
settings.description: Any monospace font. Nerd Fonts also show prompt icons.

settings.label: Size
settings.description: Ctrl+0 returns to this size.

settings.label: Weight
settings.description: How heavy normal text is. A font without that weight shows its nearest one.

settings.label: Bold weight
settings.description: How heavy bold text is.

settings.label: Ligatures
settings.description: Fonts that have them (Cascadia Code, JetBrains Mono, Fira Code) join => != -> and the like into one shape. Each character keeps its own cell, and the character under the cursor isn't joined.

settings.label: Fallback fonts
settings.description: For characters your font lacks, tried in order before Windows picks one. Separate them with commas.
settings.placeholder: Symbols Nerd Font, Noto Sans JP

settings.label: Line height
settings.description: More room between lines, as a percentage (20%) or in pixels (2). A negative value gives less. Text stays centered.

settings.label: Built-in glyphs
settings.description: Zinc draws box lines, blocks and Powerline shapes itself, so they join up in any font.

settings.label: Line thickness
settings.description: Thicker or thinner built-in lines, in pixels (1, -1) or as a percentage (20%).

settings.label: Color scheme
settings.description: About 650 are included. Add your own to the themes folder next to config.toml.

settings.label: Match 256 colors to the scheme
settings.description: Programs that use the extended 256 colors (vim and htop themes) get shades made from the scheme's 16, not the standard ones.

settings.label: Shades from background to text in light schemes
settings.description: When off, shades run from dark to light, which is what programs expect.

settings.label: Cursor text
settings.description: The character under a block cursor. If the scheme doesn't set one either, it's the background color.

settings.label: Selection
settings.description: Behind selected text. If the scheme doesn't set one either, selection inverts the colors.

settings.label: Selected text
settings.description: If the scheme doesn't set one either, the text keeps its color, or inverts with the selection when "Selection" has no color either.

settings.label: Pane headers
settings.description: Behind pane titles and tabs. On cards, the border is a step stronger.

choices.label: Same as the terminal
choices.detail: Hidden tabs get a shade instead, so the shown tab still stands out. Cards have no border.

settings.label: Minimum contrast
settings.description: Text that reads poorly against its background turns black or white. 1 turns it off, 4.5 is the usual accessibility level, and 21 makes all text black or white.

settings.label: Bold in bright colors
settings.description: Bold text in the first eight colors shows their bright versions, as older terminals did.

settings.label: Bold text color
settings.description: For bold text in the default text color.

settings.label: Faint text
settings.description: How bright dim text is (1: as bright as other text).

settings.label: Find highlight
settings.description: Behind each match of Find.

settings.label: Current match
settings.description: Behind the match Find is on.

settings.label: Cursor shape
settings.description: Until a program picks its own (vim's insert mode often does).

settings.label: Blinking cursor
settings.description: Until a program says otherwise.

settings.label: Cursor opacity
settings.description: 1: solid. Lower lets the character under a block cursor show in its own color.

settings.label: Cursor at the prompt
settings.description: While the shell waits for a command. A program's own cursor still wins. Needs shell integration.

choices.label: Bar
choices.detail: Like a text box.

settings.label: Light or dark
settings.description: Windows, menus and dialogs. The terminal keeps its color scheme. Restart Zinc to apply.

choices.label: Same as Windows
choices.detail: Windows Settings > Personalization > Colors > Choose your mode.

settings.label: Accent color
settings.description: Selections, focus lines, switches and buttons. Restart Zinc to apply.

choices.label: Windows' accent
choices.detail: The one in Windows Settings > Personalization > Colors.

settings.label: Window background
settings.description: What's behind everything in the window: tabs, sidebar and terminal.

choices.label: Mica
choices.detail: Not see-through. It takes a tint from your wallpaper, as Windows apps do.

choices.label: Acrylic (frosted)
choices.detail: The windows behind show, blurred.

choices.label: Clear
choices.detail: The windows behind show as they are.

settings.label: Window tint
settings.description: How much color an acrylic or clear background carries. Lower is more see-through.

settings.label: Window tint color
settings.description: The color an acrylic or clear background is tinted with.

settings.label: Terminal background opacity
settings.description: Lower lets the window background show behind the text (1: solid). Colored cells stay solid.

settings.label: Custom shaders
settings.description: Effects drawn over the terminal, such as CRT screens, glow and cursor trails. They're GLSL files written for Ghostty or Shadertoy, and they run in order.

settings.label: Animation
settings.description: For animated shaders. The others redraw only when the terminal changes.

choices.label: While focused
choices.detail: Unfocused, they pause where they are. The text under them still updates.

choices.label: Always
choices.detail: Every terminal with shaders keeps redrawing, focused or not.

choices.label: Never
choices.detail: They hold still, cursor effects included, and are drawn only when the terminal changes.

settings.label: Padding left and right
settings.description: Between the window's edge and the text.

settings.label: Padding top and bottom
settings.description: Between the window's edge and the text.

settings.label: Even padding
settings.description: Splits the leftover space between both sides. When off, all of it goes to the right and bottom.

settings.label: Workspaces
settings.description: Tabs along the top, or a list in a sidebar. Applies to windows opened from now on.

settings.label: Sidebar
settings.description: Only when "Workspaces" is "In a sidebar".

choices.label: Auto-hide
choices.detail: Slides out when the pointer reaches the window's left edge.

settings.label: Title bar
settings.description: Only when "Workspaces" is "In a sidebar".

choices.label: Auto-hide
choices.detail: Slides down when the pointer reaches the window's top edge.

settings.label: Start page for new workspaces
settings.description: Choose a profile, a folder and a name when you open a workspace. Enter starts the default profile.

settings.label: Colors for new workspaces
settings.description: For the ones you don't color yourself.

choices.label: By folder
choices.detail: A workspace with a folder gets that folder's color, the same one every time.

choices.label: One after another
choices.detail: Each new workspace takes the next color.

settings.label: New tabs and splits start
settings.description: New tabs in a workspace with its own folder start there. Without "Tabs inside panes", this is for splits only, because a new tab is a new workspace.

choices.label: Where you are
choices.detail: In the focused terminal's current folder.

choices.label: In the profile's folder
choices.detail: Or in the workspace's folder, when it has one.

settings.label: Tabs inside panes
settings.description: Each pane can hold several tabs.

settings.label: Show pane tabs as
settings.description: Only with "Tabs inside panes" on.

choices.label: Tabs
choices.detail: A row of tabs. When they don't fit, they shorten, then show only their icons, then fold into a menu.

choices.label: A menu
choices.detail: The shown tab, then a count ("2 of 5") that opens a menu of every tab. Switch tabs with the menu or with keys.

settings.label: Pane headers
settings.description: The row above a pane. Its tabs, or its title when it has one tab.

choices.label: Automatic
choices.detail: On every pane once a workspace is split, and on any pane with two or more tabs.

choices.label: With several tabs
choices.detail: On panes with two or more tabs.

settings.label: Header buttons
settings.description: Split, maximize and more on the right of a pane's header, with a program's progress beside them.

choices.label: Always
choices.detail: On every pane.

choices.label: Focused pane
choices.detail: On the focused pane, and on the others while the pointer is over their header.

choices.label: On hover
choices.detail: On a pane while the pointer is over its header. Touch and pen have no hover. The command palette and a pane's right-click menu have every action.

settings.label: Gap between panes
settings.description: Above 0, panes are rounded cards with space between them. At 0 they meet at a thin divider.

settings.label: Gap at the workspace edges
settings.description: The same gap around the outside, split or not, so splitting never moves a pane's outer edges. Only with a "Gap between panes" above 0.

settings.label: Show focus with
settings.description: How the focused pane stands out from the others.

choices.label: Ring
choices.detail: An accent-colored outline around the focused pane.

choices.label: Tab accent
choices.detail: An accent-colored line along the top of the focused pane.

choices.label: None
choices.detail: Only the dimming of other panes ("Unfocused panes") marks the focused pane. With "Unfocused panes" at 1, nothing does.

settings.label: Pane animations
settings.description: Panes slide into place when you split, close, maximize or move them. They don't while "Animation effects" is off in Windows Settings.

settings.label: Resize step
settings.description: How far a resize key moves the divider, as a share of the panes it splits.

settings.label: Unfocused panes
settings.description: How bright unfocused panes stay (1: not dimmed).

settings.label: Dimming color
settings.description: What unfocused panes fade toward.

settings.label: Divider color
settings.description: The line between split panes, when "Gap between panes" is 0.

settings.label: Reopen windows
settings.description: Windows, workspaces, splits and tabs come back in their folders.

choices.label: Automatic
choices.detail: While the quick terminal's hotkey is set, it stays in the tray so the hotkey keeps working. Otherwise it quits.

choices.label: Stay in the tray
choices.detail: Click the tray icon to open a window again.

settings.label: When you sign in to Windows

choices.label: Start in the tray
choices.detail: No window opens. The quick terminal's hotkey works, and the tray icon opens your windows.

choices.label: Open my windows
choices.detail: As they were when you left, or a new one.

settings.label: Open in Zinc from File Explorer
settings.description: Adds "Open in Zinc" to the right-click menu of folders and drives. On Windows 11 it's under "Show more options".

settings.label: Ask before closing
settings.description: When a tab, pane, workspace or window you close still runs a command, or holds two or more tabs. Zinc knows a command is running through shell integration.

settings.label: Ask before quitting with a running command
settings.description: When you quit Zinc (or restart it for an update) while a command still runs.

settings.label: Shell integration
settings.description: Marks prompts and commands in PowerShell, bash and zsh (WSL too), so you can jump between prompts, copy a command's output and see which commands failed.

settings.label: Command marks
settings.description: The bar beside a command's output.

choices.label: Close if it succeeded
choices.detail: A failure stays on screen so you can read why. Any key closes it.

choices.label: Keep it open
choices.detail: Any key closes it.

settings.label: Pick up environment changes
settings.description: New tabs read PATH and other variables from Windows as they start, so an installer's changes work without restarting Zinc.

settings.label: Program titles
settings.description: Shells and programs set the tab's title (often the folder or the running command). When off, tabs show the profile's name.

settings.label: Folder and command as the title
settings.description: The folder at the prompt, the running command otherwise. A program's own title still wins. Needs shell integration.

settings.label: Scrollback lines
settings.description: How far back you can scroll.

settings.label: Word boundaries
settings.description: Characters that end a word when you double-click (space and tab always do). Empty: the ones shown.

settings.label: Click to move the cursor
settings.description: At a shell prompt, clicking in the command you're typing moves the cursor there. Needs shell integration.

settings.label: Right-click
settings.description: Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the menu anywhere.

choices.label: Menu
choices.detail: Copy, paste, find, the link or command you clicked, split and close.

choices.label: Copy or paste
choices.detail: Copies a selection, or pastes when there's none.

settings.label: Open links with
settings.description: Web links and files shown in the terminal.

choices.label: Ctrl+click
choices.detail: Holding Ctrl underlines the links.

choices.label: Alt+click
choices.detail: Holding Alt underlines the links.

choices.label: A click
choices.detail: Dragging across a link still selects it. A program using the mouse still gets the click.

settings.label: Middle-click pastes
settings.description: Unless the program uses the mouse.

settings.label: Focus follows mouse
settings.description: Moving the pointer into a pane focuses it.

settings.label: Copy on select
settings.description: Copies text as soon as you select it. The selection stays.

settings.label: Copy with formatting
settings.description: Copies colors and styles too, for documents and email. Apps that take plain text still get plain text.

settings.label: Paste warning
settings.description: Ask before pasting text with more than one line.

choices.label: Automatic
choices.detail: When the program would take each line as Enter and run it. A program that marks pastes (bracketed paste) gets no warning.

choices.label: Always
choices.detail: Whenever a paste has more than one line.

settings.label: Large pastes
settings.description: Ask before pasting more than 5 KB.

settings.label: Programs may copy
settings.description: Copying with OSC 52, as tmux, neovim and remote shells do.

settings.label: Programs reading the clipboard
settings.description: Anything running, including a remote host, could read it.

choices.label: Ask each time
choices.detail: Allow once, for the tab, or not.

settings.label: Bell
settings.description: When a program rings it, e.g. at a failed tab completion.

choices.label: Tab dot
choices.detail: A dot on its tab, and the taskbar button flashes, when you aren't looking at that pane.

choices.label: Flash the pane
choices.detail: Marks the tab too.

settings.label: Bell sound
settings.description: Plays Windows' default sound too.

settings.label: Visual bell
settings.description: Programs that flash the screen instead of beeping (Git Bash does) ring Zinc's bell, as set in "Bell".

settings.label: Remote control
settings.description: Lets zn, Zinc's command-line tool, open, arrange and close tabs, type into them and read them. Any program running as you could use it.

settings.label: Use zn in other terminals
settings.description: Adds zn to your PATH, so other terminals find it too (Zinc's own terminals always do). Shells started from now on see it.

settings.label: Input methods
settings.description: Type Japanese, Chinese, Korean and more with Windows' input methods (IME). Turn it off if keys behave oddly.

settings.label: Check for updates automatically
settings.description: Once a day. New versions download in the background, and you choose when to restart. Only for Zinc installed with its installer.

settings.label: Debug log
settings.description: Keeps a record of what Zinc does, to send with a bug report. Turn it on, make the problem happen, then copy the log.

settings.label: Low-latency drawing
settings.description: What you type shows up about one screen refresh sooner. Turn it off if a terminal draws wrong or stops drawing, and tell us. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

settings.label: Free memory of hidden tabs
settings.description: Background tabs, minimized windows and the dismissed quick terminal give back their graphics memory and rebuild it when you return. Turn it off if switching tabs flashes. Only with "Low-latency drawing".

settings.label: Free it after
settings.description: Seconds, or with a unit: 45s, 2m.

settings.label: Software rendering
settings.description: Draws with the processor instead of the graphics card, which is slower. Use it for broken graphics drivers, some virtual machines and remote desktop glitches. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

settings.label: Long command finishes
settings.description: In a pane you weren't looking at.

choices.label: Tab dot
choices.detail: A dot on its tab. The taskbar button also flashes if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Notification
choices.detail: A dot on its tab, and a Windows notification if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Always notify
choices.detail: A Windows notification whenever you aren't looking at that pane, even in Zinc.

choices.label: None
choices.detail: No dot, no notification.

settings.label: Counts as long after
settings.description: Seconds, or with a unit: 45s, 2m.

settings.label: Sound
settings.description: Plays when a long command finishes out of view (a Windows notification has its own).

settings.label: Program notifications
settings.description: When a program asks for one, e.g. a build script finishing (OSC 9 or 777).

choices.label: Tab dot
choices.detail: A dot on its tab. The taskbar button also flashes if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Notification
choices.detail: A dot on its tab, and a Windows notification if Zinc is in the background.

choices.label: Always notify
choices.detail: A Windows notification whenever you aren't looking at that pane, even in Zinc.

choices.label: None
choices.detail: No dot, no notification.

settings.label: Finished
settings.description: A command finished, or a program sent a notification.

settings.label: Bell
settings.description: A program rang the bell.

settings.label: Failed
settings.description: A command failed, or a program exited with an error.

settings.label: Hotkey
settings.description: Shows and hides the quick terminal from anywhere, e.g. win+grave or ctrl+alt+t.

choices.label: With the pointer
choices.detail: Opens on the screen the pointer is on.

choices.label: Main
choices.detail: Always opens on the main screen.

settings.label: Size
settings.description: A percentage or pixels (50%, 600px) along its edge. Empty: 50%, or 70% by 60% at "Center".

settings.label: Animation
settings.description: How long the quick terminal takes to fade in and out. At 0 it appears at once.

settings.label: SSH hosts
settings.description: From ~/.ssh/config.

fileOnly.text: Palette colors by number (palette.1 = "#AC4242") are set in config.toml.
Folders of shaders to choose from. Add and remove them on the shaders page (the library's … menu).
